config.title: useSyncExternalStore

intro.title: useSyncExternalStore
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React component that displays a real-time counter, updated from an external store. You will learn how to use the useSyncExternalStore hook to subscribe to changes in external data sources and keep your UI in sync. The main technologies involved are React hooks, JavaScript functions, and a basic external store object. This beginner-friendly lesson will help you understand how to integrate external state into your React applications efficiently.
intro.usecase: useSyncExternalStore is essential for connecting React components to external state sources like browser APIs, third-party libraries, or custom stores. You'll use it in dashboard applications that need to sync with real-time data streams, such as live financial charts or collaborative editing tools. It's also crucial for implementing responsive UI components that react to browser events like network status changes or viewport resizing. This hook allows you to create seamless integrations with non-React systems while maintaining React's declarative programming model.

objectives: Implement a basic external store using a simple JavaScript object
Configure a React component to subscribe to external store changes
Initialize useSyncExternalStore with subscription and getSnapshot functions
Render component state that automatically updates when the external store changes
Manipulate external store data and observe synchronized component updates
Integrate useSyncExternalStore with custom event listeners for store changes
Construct a complete example with external store, subscription, and React component synchronization

steps.title: Import React and useSyncExternalStore
steps.instruction: Import React and the useSyncExternalStore hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and useSyncExternalStore from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have access to React and the useSyncExternalStore hook for building your component.
successCriteria: React and useSyncExternalStore are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useSyncExternalStore from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and useSyncExternalStore from 'react'.

steps.title: Create a simple external store
steps.instruction: Define a simple external store object named 'store' with a 'value' property set to 0 and a 'subscribe' function that accepts a callback parameter.
steps.hint: Create a plain JavaScript object with a 'value' property and a 'subscribe' method that takes a callback.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a basic store object with a numeric value and a subscription function, which is the foundation for using useSyncExternalStore.
successCriteria: A 'store' object is defined with a 'value' property set to 0 and a 'subscribe' method that accepts a callback parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your store object has both a 'value' property and a 'subscribe' function that accepts a callback.
steps.feedbackWrong: Please create a store object with a 'value' property and a 'subscribe' function. Both are needed for the next steps.

steps.title: Create the main component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns an empty fragment for now.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function named App that returns <> </>.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an App component defined that returns an empty fragment.
successCriteria: A functional component named App is defined and returns an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main App component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a component named App that returns an empty fragment (<> </>).
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't defined correctly. Create a function named App that returns an empty fragment.

steps.title: Initialize state with useSyncExternalStore
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, call useSyncExternalStore with the store's subscribe function and a getSnapshot function that returns the store's current value.
steps.hint: The subscribe function is store.subscribe. The getSnapshot function should return store.getSnapshot().
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will subscribe to the external store and get its current snapshot value.
successCriteria: useSyncExternalStore is called with store.subscribe and a function that returns store.getSnapshot().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're passing store.subscribe as the first argument and a function that returns store.getSnapshot() as the second argument.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try calling useSyncExternalStore with store.subscribe and a function that returns store.getSnapshot().

steps.title: Display the store value
steps.instruction: In the component's JSX, add a paragraph element that displays the value returned by useSyncExternalStore.
steps.hint:
You can use a

tag and reference the variable where you stored the snapshot value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a value in JSX

Current count: {count}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show the store value (currently 0) in a paragraph below the heading.
successCriteria: A paragraph element displays the snapshot value from useSyncExternalStore.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're displaying the snapshot value in a paragraph element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph element is missing or not displaying the snapshot value correctly.

steps.title: Add a button to increment the store value
steps.instruction: Define an increment function inside the App component that updates the store's value property and notifies subscribers.
steps.hint: Create a function that increases store.value by 1 and calls any subscribed callbacks.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now contains an increment function that modifies the store's value.
successCriteria: An increment function is defined inside the App component that updates store.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function updates store.value and would notify subscribers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The increment function isn't defined correctly. It should update store.value.

steps.title: Wire the increment button
steps.instruction: Add a button element with an onClick handler that calls the increment function inside the return statement of your App component.
steps.hint: Place a <button> element within the <div> and set its onClick prop to call the increment function you'll define later.
steps.expectedOutcome: A button element appears in the UI that will trigger the increment function when clicked.
successCriteria: A <button> element with an onClick handler that calls the increment function is added to the return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has an onClick handler that calls the increment function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding a <button> element with an onClick handler inside the <div> in the return statement.

steps.title: Add a button to decrement the store value
steps.instruction: Inside your component, define a function named 'decrement' that decreases the store's value by 1 and notifies subscribers.
steps.hint: Create a function that modifies the store.value property and calls any subscribed listeners.
steps.expectedOutcome: A decrement function is defined that will update the store's value.
successCriteria: The decrement function is defined and modifies store.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it decreases store.value by 1.
steps.feedbackWrong: The decrement function isn't defined correctly. It should modify store.value.

steps.title: Wire the decrement button
steps.instruction: Add a second button element with an onClick handler that calls the decrement function in your component's return statement.
steps.hint: Place the button after the increment button. Use onClick={decrement} to connect it to your decrement function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with an onClick handler
<button onClick={decrement}>Decrement</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A decrement button appears in the UI that will call the decrement function when clicked.
successCriteria: The component's return statement includes a button element with onClick={decrement}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has onClick={decrement} to properly wire it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The decrement button is missing or not properly connected. Add a button with onClick={decrement}.

steps.title: Add a reset button
steps.instruction: Define a reset function inside your App component that sets the store's value back to 0 and notifies subscribers.
steps.hint: Create a function named reset that updates store.value to 0, then calls any subscribed listeners.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a reset function that resets the store's value to 0 and triggers subscriber notifications.
successCriteria: A reset function is defined inside the App component that sets store.value to 0 and calls subscribed listeners.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your reset function both sets store.value to 0 and notifies subscribers.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a function named reset that updates store.value to 0 and calls any subscribed listeners.
